summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators (AWS, Azure, Google) that let corporations access multiple foundation models through a single secure, managed API without data leaving their governed cloud boundary. There is no universal winner — the best fit is driven by existing cloud footprint, required model breadth, and compliance posture. Data-platform players (Snowflake, Databricks) and IBM watsonx extend this to bring AI directly to governed enterprise data, while edge-focused options like Cloudflare Workers AI target low-latency, globally distributed inference.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy — inference runs inside the company's own cloud tenant/VPC so prompts, outputs, and proprietary data never leave the governed boundary or train external models.

Compliance and governance — aggregators inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR, EU data boundary) and provide audit logs, IAM, and region pinning out of the box.
Single billing and existing contracts — consumption is billed through an existing cloud agreement (EDP/MACC commitments), consolidating procurement, spend commitments, and vendor management.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in — one API provides access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, and others, so teams can swap or benchmark models without re-architecting integrations.

Enterprise security and operations — centralized identity, private networking (VPC/PrivateLink), guardrails/content filtering, throughput reservations, and integration with existing observability and DevSecOps tooling.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput reservations for guaranteed capacity; batch pricing available. Billed via AWS account.
key_features: No data used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS that want the widest third-party model choice behind one API with mature security tooling.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: OpenAI GPT image and embedding models
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (standard) and Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed via Azure/EA agreement.
key_features: Content filtering and responsible AI guardrails
Data not used to train OpenAI models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops needing first-party OpenAI models with enterprise governance and deep Azure/M365 integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand; Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units, e.g. ~25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained). Billed via GCP account.
key_features: Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Data/analytics-heavy and Google Cloud organizations wanting Gemini plus a broad model garden with strong MLOps and grounding.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits (compute), metered by tokens/function calls; billed via existing Snowflake contract.
key_features: Models run next to governed data in Snowflake
Role-based access control inheriting data governance
No data movement out of the warehouse
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data already lives in Snowflake and want AI on governed data without moving it out.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
available_models: OpenAI / external models via Model Serving
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving and training; pay-per-token for foundation model APIs; billed via Databricks/cloud contract.
key_features: Model Serving with external model gateway
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams building custom models and RAG on a governed lakehouse.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus token/resource-unit consumption; available SaaS or on-prem/hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and auditability
watsonx Orchestrate for enterprise agent management across platforms
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid/on-prem shops needing strong AI governance, agent orchestration, and IBM indemnification.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI cluster hosting for reserved capacity; billed via OCI account.
platforms.best_for: Oracle ERP/database customers and sovereignty-focused organizations wanting GenAI close to Oracle workloads.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: Various open-source LLMs and embedding models
AI Gateway proxy to external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
compliance: Data Localization Suite for region control
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use (neurons/tokens) on the Workers platform; low entry cost, no reserved commitment required.
key_features: Globally distributed edge inference for low latency
AI Gateway with caching, rate limiting and logging
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference at the edge and a unified gateway to many providers.
